info.name: Prafi API
info.description:
Backend API (Express + Sequelize + PostgreSQL).

**Setup (once)**
1. Import this collection and `Prafi-Local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select **Prafi Local** in the environment dropdown (top right).
3. In **Prafi Local**, set `superadminPassword` (same as SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env) in the **Current value** column, then Ctrl+S.

**Automatic saving**: after every Login, the token is saved to the environment as `{{token}}` (last logged-in user) and `{{superadminToken}}` / `{{adminToken}}` / `{{tenantToken}}`. Register and Upload save `adminEmail`, `tenantEmail`, `imageId`, `imageUrl`. Each save is printed in the Postman Console. Scripts write the environment **Current value** (Initial value stays empty on purpose).

**Collection Runner**: turn on *Keep variable values* (Persist responses / variables) so values from the run stay in the environment afterwards.

**Roles**: superadmin → can create admin, admin → can create tenant.

**Responses**: `{ success: true, data }` or `{ success: false, error: { code, message, details? } }`.

**Activation**: new admin/tenant accounts must be activated before they can log in (the collection does this right after each Register).

**Token**: every request uses `{{token}}` (collection → Authorization), which each Login request sets to the account that just logged in. Log in as the role a request needs first — the request names say which, e.g. "(by Superadmin)", "(tenant)", "(admin)". The role tokens (`superadminToken`, `adminToken`, `tenantToken`) are still saved, but no request uses them.

**Tokens**: role-specific requests use their own token (`{{superadminToken}}`, `{{adminToken}}`, `{{tenantToken}}`). Requests without their own auth (Me, Update Me, List Users) use the collection default `{{token}}` = whoever logged in last.

variable.description: Password given to users created by the Register requests

exec: var save = (key, value) => { pm.environment.set(key, value); pm.collectionVariables.set(key, value); console.log('saved {{' + key + '}}'); };
try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { /* not JSON, e.g. an image */ }
if (body) pm.test('Response is JSON with a success flag', () => pm.expect(body).to.have.property('success'));
// Any login response: keep the token for that role + as {{token}} (the last logged-in user)

item.name: 2. Images
item.description: Upload an image first; its id is used as faceImageId when registering a user.

formdata.description: jpg / png / webp / gif, max 5 MB
Optional, defaults to the file name

request.description:
Any logged-in user. Multipart field `image` (max 5 MB, jpg/png/webp/gif) + optional `altText`.

The returned `id` is saved to `{{imageId}}` (used by *Register - Tenant*), `url` to `{{imageUrl}}`.

**In Postman desktop:** re-select the file in the `image` row (Postman can't store local file paths across machines) — a sample is in `postman/sample-face.png`.

Errors: 400 missing/wrong file type, 413 file larger than 5 MB.

item.name: Register - Tenant with face image (by Admin)

request.description:
Requires **admin** token. An admin can only create `tenant` accounts.

Run **Images / Upload Image** first — its `id` is saved to `{{imageId}}` and used as `faceImageId` here. Each image can belong to only one user (409 otherwise).

request.description:
New accounts cannot log in until activated. Activates the tenant created above (`{{tenantId}}`).

Body: `isActive` (true/false, required), `role` (required — must match the user's actual role; it is a safety check and never changes the role), `reason` (optional, defaults to "Activated by <role>").

Rules: superadmin → admin and tenant accounts, admin → tenant accounts. Nobody can change the superadmin. Takes effect immediately, even for tokens already issued.
Logs in as the tenant created above. The token is saved to `{{tenantToken}}`. Also saved to `{{token}}` (the last logged-in user).
Any logged-in user. Returns the profile including `faceImage` (with its full `url`).

Any logged-in user updates **their own** account . There is no id in the URL, so nobody can update another user.

Send only the fields to change:
- `firstName`, `lastName`, `phoneNumber`, `email` (non-empty strings; email must be unique)
- `faceImageId`: id from **Upload Image**, or `null` to remove it (each image belongs to one user)
- `password` (min 8) **together with** `currentPassword`

Not allowed (400): `id`, `role`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, unknown fields, empty body.

Errors: 400 validation / wrong currentPassword, 401 no token, 409 email or faceImageId used by another user.

**Changing your password here does not update `{{newUserPassword}}`**, so the Login requests for this user will fail until you change it back or update that variable.

query.description: Optional filter; must be a role you are allowed to see

request.description:
One route, result depends on who calls it :

- **superadmin** → all accounts (superadmin, admin, tenant)
- **admin** → tenant accounts only
- **tenant** → 403 (tenants only have **Me**)

Query: `page` (default 1), `limit` (default 20, max 100), `role` (optional filter). Response: `data` = users (with `faceImage`), `meta` = `{ page, limit, total, totalPages }`.

exec: pm.test('Returns a list with paging meta', () => { pm.expect(body.data).to.be.an('array'); pm.expect(body.meta).to.have.property('total'); });

item.name: 5. Approvals
item.description: Activate / deactivate **tenant accounts**: `PATCH /api/approvals/:userId?type=user` (superadmin → admin and tenant accounts, admin → tenant accounts). Runs in order: deactivate the tenant, show it is blocked, activate it again (so later requests keep working). Product activation is in **6. Products**.

request.description:
Body: `isActive` (true/false, required), `role` (required — must match the user's actual role; it is a safety check and never changes the role), `reason` (optional, defaults to "Activated by <role>").

Rules: superadmin → admin and tenant accounts, admin → tenant accounts. Nobody can change the superadmin. Takes effect immediately, even for tokens already issued.
The tenant was just deactivated, so logging in is refused with 403 `USER_NOT_ACTIVATED` (tokens issued before are rejected too).
Negative example: an admin may only change tenant accounts, so this returns 403 (also for its own account).
Logs in as the superadmin so the next requests (which all use `{{token}}`) run as that user.

Superadmin can activate/deactivate tenants too.

Body: `isActive` (true/false, required), `role` (required — must match the user's actual role; it is a safety check and never changes the role), `reason` (optional, defaults to "Activated by <role>").

Rules: superadmin → admin and tenant accounts, admin → tenant accounts. Nobody can change the superadmin. Takes effect immediately, even for tokens already issued.

item.name: 6. Products
item.description:
Product CRUD. Rules: only **tenants** create/update/delete, and only **their own** products. **superadmin/admin** can read every product (and activate/deactivate it), but not create/update/delete.

Runs in order: tenant uploads an image → creates a product (starts **inactive**, `approval.isActive = false`) → reads/updates it → admin lists pending products and activates it → superadmin deactivates it → tenant deletes it.

request.description: Logs in as the tenant so the next requests (which all use `{{token}}`) run as that user.

item.name: 7. Cleanup & Logout
item.description: Deletes the uploaded image, then logs out every role (tenant, admin, superadmin) and checks each logged-out token is rejected. Run this folder last: after it, every saved token is revoked, so run the Login requests again before other requests.

request.description: Requires **tenant** role (current rule in `image.routes.ts`). Deletes the DB row and the file. Users using this image get `faceImageId = null`.

Any role (superadmin, admin, tenant). Revokes the token sent with this request: it is rejected from now on, even before it expires. Only this token is logged out, the user's other sessions (other devices/logins) keep working. Logging out the same token twice returns 401. After logging out, run the matching Login request to get a new token.
The tenant's logged-out token now gets 401 "Token has been revoked".
Logs in as the admin so the next requests (which all use `{{token}}`) run as that user.

Logs in as the superadmin so the next requests (which all use `{{token}}`) run as that user.
